title: Сломанный нос и звонок от мамы  (The Broken Nose and the Call from Mom)

segments.t: Backed into a corner by Nastya's questions, Kostya sheepishly confesses that while trying to make peace with her father, he accidentally broke the man's nose. Nastya is furious with Kostya for beating up her father a second time, and seconds later her mother calls with news of the injury.
Костя, может, ты маму мою тоже и забьешь?
И вообще, похоже, я тебя плохо знала.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'Nastya, just promise you will not get upset.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Nastya' before landing on 'worry'.
'I am not getting upset.' Nastya brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'not' in a few short words.
'I really wanted to help you make peace.' Kostya anchors the line on 'I', while 'you' completes the thought. Nastya answers right away.
'And I broke his nose.' In Russian, the idea of 'broke' flows naturally into 'nose' without extra filler words.
'Did the two of you get into a fight again?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'you' before landing on 'to fight'.
'He barely even fought back.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to fight', turning the action back on the subject. Kostya answers right away.
'He was the one who told me to swing.' The meaning hinges on 'but' working together with 'suggested' in spoken Russian.
'And you beat the man up.' Nastya anchors the line on 'both', while 'a person' completes the thought.
'Well, he asked for it himself.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to want' places the action in the masculine past tense. Nastya answers right away.
Костя, может, ты маму мою тоже и забьешь?
'Kostya, maybe you are going to beat up my mother next?' In Russian, the idea of 'Kostya' flows naturally into 'to score' without extra filler words.
И вообще, похоже, я тебя плохо знала.
'Honestly, it seems I hardly knew you at all.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'both' before landing on 'knew'.
'Hello, Mom, what happened to Dad?' Notice how Russian expresses 'hello' and 'dad' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Kostya answers right away.
'All right, I am on my way right now.' The meaning hinges on 'like this' working together with 'to arrive' in spoken Russian. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Костя, может, ты маму мою тоже и забьешь?
И вообще, похоже, я тебя плохо знала.
